title: Client-specific interfaces
questions:
  - id: definition
    prompt: What does the Interface Segregation Principle state?
    options:
      - text: Every class must implement exactly one interface
      - id: clients
        text: Clients should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use
        correct: true
      - text: Interfaces must live in a separate assembly from their implementations
      - text: Interfaces should never inherit from other interfaces
    explanation: Fat interfaces couple clients to members they never call, so changes to those members ripple into unrelated clients.
  - id: who-owns
    prompt: Who should an interface be shaped around?
    options:
      - text: The class that implements it
      - text: The database schema
      - id: client
        text: The client that uses it
        correct: true
    explanation: Interfaces describe what a client needs. One implementation can satisfy several client-shaped interfaces.
  - id: symptoms
    prompt: Which are symptoms of a fat interface?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: Implementations throw `NotImplementedException` for several members
        correct: true
      - text: Test doubles must stub many methods the test never touches
        correct: true
      - text: Most clients call only a small subset of the members
        correct: true
      - text: The interface has a descriptive name
    explanation: Unused members show up as stubs, throwing implementations and clients that only use a slice of the interface.
---
## Learning objectives

- State the interface segregation principle
- Split a fat interface into role interfaces
- Let one class implement several small interfaces

## A fat interface

```csharp
public interface IMultiFunctionDevice
{
    void Print(Document d);
    void Scan(Document d);
    void Fax(Document d);
    void Staple(Document d);
}

public sealed class BasicPrinter : IMultiFunctionDevice
{
    public void Print(Document d) { /* ... */ }
    public void Scan(Document d)   => throw new NotImplementedException();
    public void Fax(Document d)    => throw new NotImplementedException();
    public void Staple(Document d) => throw new NotImplementedException();
}
```

`BasicPrinter` is forced to lie, and every client that only prints still recompiles and redeploys
whenever the fax signature changes.

## Segregated interfaces

```csharp
public interface IPrinter { void Print(Document d); }
public interface IScanner { void Scan(Document d); }
public interface IFax     { void Fax(Document d); }

public sealed class BasicPrinter : IPrinter { public void Print(Document d) { } }
public sealed class OfficeMachine : IPrinter, IScanner, IFax
{
    public void Print(Document d) { }
    public void Scan(Document d) { }
    public void Fax(Document d) { }
}
```

The same `OfficeMachine` instance can be registered under several interfaces:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddSingleton<OfficeMachine>();
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IPrinter>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<OfficeMachine>());
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IScanner>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<OfficeMachine>());
```

## ISP and LSP

Fat interfaces tend to cause LSP violations, because implementations throw for members they cannot
support. Segregation removes the temptation: if you cannot fax, you simply do not implement `IFax`.

## Learning objectives

- Split repositories and services by how they are used
- Recognise role interfaces in the base class library
- Avoid over-fragmentation

## Read and write roles

```csharp
public interface IOrderReader
{
    Task<OrderDto?> FindAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct);
    Task<IReadOnlyList<OrderSummary>> ListForCustomerAsync(int customerId, CancellationToken ct);
}

public interface IOrderWriter
{
    Task<int> AddAsync(Order order, CancellationToken ct);
    Task CancelAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct);
}

public sealed class SqlOrderStore : IOrderReader, IOrderWriter { /* ... */ }
```

The reporting page asks for `IOrderReader`. It cannot accidentally write, and its tests only need
a fake with two methods.

## Interfaces in the base class library

The BCL is full of tiny role interfaces: `IDisposable` (one method), `IAsyncDisposable`,
`IComparable<T>`, `IEquatable<T>`, `IEnumerable<T>`. Their smallness is exactly why so many types
can implement them and so much generic code can rely on them.

## Interfaces shaped for consumers

```csharp
public sealed class InvoiceEmailer(IOrderReader orders, IEmailSender email)
{
    public async Task SendAsync(int orderId, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var order = await orders.FindAsync(orderId, ct) ?? throw new OrderNotFoundException(orderId);
        await email.SendAsync(order.CustomerEmail, "Your invoice", InvoiceTemplate.Render(order), ct);
    }
}
```

## Balance

Do not create an interface per method by reflex. Group members by the clients that use them
together. A good test: could you describe the interface's role in a short noun phrase —
"order reader", "email sender"? If so, it is probably the right size.

title: Inverting dependencies
questions:
  - id: definition
    prompt: Which pair of statements makes up the Dependency Inversion Principle?
    options:
      - text: Classes should create their own dependencies; dependencies should be static.
      - id: dip
        text: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules; both should depend on abstractions. Abstractions should not depend on details; details should depend on abstractions.

    explanation: This is Robert C. Martin's two-part formulation.
  - id: ownership
    prompt: In a design that follows DIP, which layer should own the `IOrderRepository` interface?

      - text: A shared "Interfaces" project referenced by everything
      - id: application

  - id: not-same
    prompt: Which statements are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: Dependency injection is a technique that helps implement dependency inversion
        correct: true

        correct: true
      - text: Using a DI container automatically means you follow DIP
      - text: "`new`-ing up a stable type like `List<T>` violates DIP"
    explanation: A container is optional plumbing. DIP is about the direction of dependencies on volatile details; stable framework types are fine to depend on directly.
---
## Learning objectives

- State the dependency inversion principle
- Explain which layer owns an abstraction
- Distinguish DIP, dependency injection and DI containers

## The problem

```csharp
public sealed class CheckoutService
{
    private readonly SqlOrderRepository _orders = new("Server=prod;...");
    private readonly StripeGateway _payments = new("sk_live_...");
}
```

Checkout — the business policy — depends on SQL Server and Stripe. To test it you need both; to
change payment providers you must edit the business logic.

## The principle

> High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions.
> Abstractions should not depend on details. Details should depend on abstractions.

```csharp
namespace Shop.Application;

public interface IOrderRepository { Task AddAsync(Order order, CancellationToken ct); }
public interface IPaymentGateway { Task<PaymentResult> ChargeAsync(Money amount, CardToken card, CancellationToken ct); }

public sealed class CheckoutService(IOrderRepository orders, IPaymentGateway payments)
{
    public async Task CheckoutAsync(Cart cart, CardToken card, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var result = await payments.ChargeAsync(cart.Total, card, ct);
        if (!result.Succeeded) throw new PaymentDeclinedException(result.Reason);
        await orders.AddAsync(Order.From(cart, result.TransactionId), ct);
    }
}
```

```csharp
namespace Shop.Infrastructure;

public sealed class StripePaymentGateway(StripeClient client) : Application.IPaymentGateway { /* ... */ }
```

## Why "inversion"

Without DIP, source-code dependencies point the same way as the flow of control: policy → detail.
With DIP, the interface lives *with the policy*, so the infrastructure project references the
application project — the source-code arrow is **inverted** against the flow of control.

## DIP, DI and containers

| Term | What it is |
|------|------------|
| Dependency inversion | A design principle about dependency *direction* |
| Dependency injection | A technique: pass dependencies in, usually through the constructor |
| DI container | A library that builds object graphs (e.g. `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`) |

You can follow DIP with plain constructor calls in `Main`. A container is a convenience.

> Do not abstract everything. `List<T>`, `string` and `DateOnly` are stable; depend on them
> directly. Invert dependencies on things that are **volatile**: databases, networks, clocks,
> file systems, third-party services.

---
title: The composition root and DI containers
questions:
  - id: composition-root
    prompt: Where should object graphs be composed in an ASP.NET Core application?

      - text: In a static `ServiceLocator` called from anywhere

        correct: true
    explanation: The composition root is the one place that knows about concrete implementations. Everywhere else depends on abstractions.
  - id: service-locator
    prompt: Why is calling `serviceProvider.GetService<T>()` from deep inside business classes considered an anti-pattern?
    options:
      - text: It is slower than reflection
      - id: hidden
        text: It hides dependencies, so a class's constructor no longer tells you what it needs
        correct: true
      - text: It is not supported in .NET 10
    explanation: Service location makes dependencies implicit, harder to test and easy to get wrong at runtime.
  - id: lifetimes
    prompt: Which statements about Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection lifetimes are true?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: A singleton is created once for the root container
        correct: true
      - text: In ASP.NET Core, a scoped service is created once per HTTP request
        correct: true
      - text: A transient service is created every time it is resolved
        correct: true
      - text: Injecting a scoped service into a singleton is always safe
    explanation: A singleton holding a scoped service keeps it alive beyond its scope — a captive dependency. Scope validation in Development detects this.
---
## Learning objectives

- Compose object graphs in a single composition root
- Avoid the service locator anti-pattern
- Pick correct lifetimes and avoid captive dependencies

## The composition root

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddScoped<IOrderRepository, SqlOrderRepository>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IPaymentGateway, StripePaymentGateway>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<CheckoutService>();
builder.Services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);

var app = builder.Build();
app.MapPost("/checkout", (CheckoutRequest req, CheckoutService checkout, CancellationToken ct) =>
    checkout.CheckoutAsync(req.Cart, req.Card, ct));
app.Run();
```

Only `Program.cs` knows that `IPaymentGateway` means Stripe. Swapping providers is a one-line change.

## Lifetimes

| Lifetime | Created | Typical use |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| Singleton | Once | Stateless services, caches, `TimeProvider` |
| Scoped | Once per scope (per request in ASP.NET Core) | `DbContext`, unit of work |
| Transient | Every resolution | Lightweight stateless helpers |

A **captive dependency** happens when a longer-lived service holds a shorter-lived one, such as a
singleton holding a `DbContext`. ASP.NET Core enables scope validation in the Development
environment, which throws when a scoped service is resolved from the root provider.

## Service locator

```csharp
public sealed class CheckoutService(IServiceProvider services)
{
    public Task CheckoutAsync(Cart cart) =>
        services.GetRequiredService<IPaymentGateway>().ChargeAsync(/* ... */);
}
```

The constructor lies about what the class needs. Ask for `IPaymentGateway` directly instead.
Resolving from `IServiceProvider` is acceptable only in infrastructure code such as factories and
middleware, where creating scopes is the actual job.

FILE: content/books/solid-principles/07-solid-in-practice/01-case-study.md

---
title: "Case study: a notification service"
questions:
  - id: which-principle
    prompt: Adding SMS by writing a new `SmsChannel` class and registering it, without editing `NotificationService`, demonstrates which principle most directly?
    options:
      - text: Single Responsibility
      - text: Liskov Substitution
      - text: Interface Segregation
      - id: ocp
        text: Open/Closed
        correct: true
    explanation: The service gains behaviour through a new implementation, while existing code stays closed to modification.
  - id: lsp-check
    prompt: "`PushChannel.SendAsync` silently does nothing when the user has no device registered, while other channels throw. Which principle is at risk?"
    options:
      - text: Dependency Inversion, because push notifications use a third-party SDK
      - id: lsp
        text: Liskov Substitution, because channels behave inconsistently under the same contract
        correct: true
      - text: None — implementation details do not matter
    explanation: Callers of `INotificationChannel` need one predictable contract. Make "cannot deliver" explicit, for example by returning a result.
  - id: benefits
    prompt: Which benefits came from the refactoring in this case study?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: Each channel can be unit tested in isolation
        correct: true
      - text: The service can be tested with fake channels and no network
        correct: true
      - text: New channels require no changes to the dispatcher
        correct: true
      - text: The number of classes in the system decreased
    explanation: The design traded a few more types for isolation, testability and extensibility.
---
## Learning objectives

- Apply the five principles together on a realistic example
- Recognise which principle each design decision supports

## Before

```csharp
public class NotificationService
{
    public void Notify(User user, string message)
    {
        if (user.PrefersEmail)
            new SmtpClient("smtp.example.com").Send("noreply@example.com", user.Email, "Notice", message);
        else if (user.PrefersSms)
            TwilioClient.Send(user.Phone, message);
        File.AppendAllText("notifications.log", $"{DateTime.Now}: {user.Id} {message}\n");
    }
}
```

## After

```csharp
public sealed record DeliveryResult(bool Delivered, string? Reason = null);

public interface INotificationChannel
{
    string Name { get; }
    bool CanDeliverTo(User user);
    Task<DeliveryResult> SendAsync(User user, string message, CancellationToken ct);
}

public sealed class EmailChannel(IEmailSender sender) : INotificationChannel
{
    public string Name => "email";
    public bool CanDeliverTo(User user) => user.PrefersEmail && user.Email is not null;
    public async Task<DeliveryResult> SendAsync(User user, string message, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        await sender.SendAsync(user.Email!, "Notice", message, ct);
        return new DeliveryResult(true);
    }
}

public sealed partial class NotificationService(
    IEnumerable<INotificationChannel> channels,
    ILogger<NotificationService> logger)
{
    public async Task NotifyAsync(User user, string message, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        foreach (var channel in channels.Where(c => c.CanDeliverTo(user)))
        {
            var result = await channel.SendAsync(user, message, ct);
            LogDelivery(user.Id, channel.Name, result.Delivered);
        }
    }

    [LoggerMessage(Level = LogLevel.Information, Message = "Notified {UserId} via {Channel}: {Delivered}")]
    private partial void LogDelivery(int userId, string channel, bool delivered);
}
```

## Mapping decisions to principles

| Decision | Principle |
|----------|-----------|
| Each channel has its own class | SRP |
| New channels are new classes plus a registration | OCP |
| Every channel returns a `DeliveryResult` instead of throwing or silently skipping | LSP |
| `IEmailSender` exposes only sending, not mailbox management | ISP |
| `NotificationService` depends on interfaces composed in `Program.cs` | DIP |

FILE: content/books/solid-principles/07-solid-in-practice/02-pitfalls-and-balance.md
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
---
title: Pitfalls and balance
questions:
  - id: yagni
    prompt: You are writing the first and only implementation of a report exporter, and there is no known need for another. What is the most pragmatic choice?
    options:
      - text: Create an interface, an abstract base class, a factory and a plugin loader up front
      - text: Put the exporter code directly in the controller
      - id: simple
        text: Write the concrete class cleanly and extract an abstraction when a second need appears
        correct: true
    explanation: YAGNI — "you aren't gonna need it". Clean concrete code is easy to refactor later; speculative abstractions cost something every day.
  - id: header-interfaces
    prompt: What is a "header interface"?
    options:
      - id: mirror
        text: An interface that mirrors every public member of a single class, created by reflex rather than from client needs
        correct: true
      - text: An interface that only declares properties
      - text: An interface declared at the top of a file
    explanation: Header interfaces add indirection without providing a real abstraction. They often violate ISP because they are shaped around the implementation.
  - id: when-apply
    prompt: Which situations justify investing in SOLID-style abstractions?
    type: multiple
    options:
      - text: The code talks to volatile infrastructure such as databases, queues or third-party APIs
        correct: true
      - text: There are already two or three variations of the same behaviour
        correct: true
      - text: You need to unit test business rules without real infrastructure
        correct: true
      - text: A one-off script that will be deleted next week
    explanation: Abstractions pay for themselves where change, variation or testing pressure exists.
---
## Learning objectives

- Recognise over-engineering driven by SOLID
- Apply YAGNI and the rule of three
- Decide when an abstraction pays for itself

## Over-engineering

The most common failure with SOLID is not ignoring it — it is applying it everywhere:

```csharp
public interface IStringFormatterFactoryProvider
{
    IStringFormatterFactory GetFactory(FormatterKind kind);
}
```

If there is one formatter and no plan for another, every reader now navigates three files to
discover that a string is upper-cased.

## Useful counterweights

| Heuristic | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| YAGNI | Do not build for needs you do not have yet |
| Rule of three | Extract an abstraction on the third repetition, not the first |
| KISS | The simplest design that works is usually the right first design |
| Keep things that change together, together | Cohesion beats fragmentation |

## Header interfaces

Creating `IFoo` for every `Foo`, with identical members, is a ritual, not a design. Abstractions
should come from **clients** (ISP) and from **volatility** (DIP). Modern mocking libraries and
in-memory fakes mean you rarely need an interface purely for testing a stable, pure class.

## A practical checklist

- Does this code depend on something volatile? → invert the dependency
- Do I already have variations? → introduce a strategy or polymorphism
- Would a change requested by one group break another? → split responsibilities
- Are implementations throwing for members they cannot support? → segregate interfaces
- None of the above? → write clear, concrete code and move on

> SOLID is a means to an end: code that is easy to understand, test and change.

## Errata that affect this section

- Page 131 — the claim that hydrogen "gradually leaks out of any practical container" (with the one-week parking example) is incorrect. title: "Fission, fusion, and beautifully small streams"
questions:
- id: q1
  prompt: Who said lumping nuclear energy in with nuclear weapons was as big a mistake as lumping in nuclear medicine?
  options:
  - text: Jonathon Porritt
  - text: David King
  - text: "Patrick Moore, former Director of Greenpeace International"
    correct: true
  - text: James Lovelock
  explanation: "**p. 161:** “We made the mistake of lumping nuclear energy in with nuclear weapons … Patrick Moore, former Director of Greenpeace International”."
- id: q2
  prompt: What distinguishes fission from fusion?
  options:
  - text: Fission uses hydrogen; fusion uses uranium
  - text: They are the same process
  - text: Fission happens only in the sun
  - text: Fission splits heavy nuclei (e.g. uranium); fusion fuses light nuclei (e.g. hydrogen)
    correct: true
  explanation: "**p. 161:** “Fission reactions split up heavy nuclei into medium-sized nuclei, releasing energy. Fusion reactions fuse light nuclei into medium-sized nuclei, releasing energy.”"
- id: q3
  prompt: How does nuclear energy per atom compare with chemical energy per atom?
  options:
  - text: About the same
  - text: About ten times bigger
  - text: About a thousand times smaller
  - text: Roughly one million times bigger
    correct: true
  explanation: "**p. 161:** “the nuclear energy available per atom is roughly one million times bigger than the chemical energy per atom of typical fuels.”"
- id: q4
  prompt: "What mass of fossil fuel does the average Brit consume daily, and what waste does it make?"
  type: multiple
  options:
  - text: About 1.6 kg per day
  - text: About 30 kg of CO2 per day (11 tons per year)
    correct: true
  - text: "About 16 kg per day (4 kg coal, 4 kg oil, 8 kg gas)"
    correct: true
  - text: About 300 kg of CO2 per day
  explanation: "**p. 161:** “The mass of the fossil fuels consumed by ‘the average British person’ is about 16 kg per day (4 kg of coal, 4 kg of oil, and 8 kg of gas) … creates 11 tons per year of waste carbon dioxide; that’s 30 kg per day.”"
- id: q5
  prompt: How much natural uranium provides the same energy as 16 kg of fossil fuels in a standard reactor?
  options:
  - text: "2 grams, producing a quarter of a gram of waste"
    correct: true
  - text: "2 kilograms"
  - text: "0.002 grams"
  - text: "16 grams"
  explanation: "**p. 161:** “the amount of natural uranium required … is 2 grams; and the resulting waste weighs one quarter of a gram.”"
- id: q6
  prompt: Why is the 2 g not one millionth of 16 kg?
  options:
  - text: "Today's reactors burn up less than 1% of the uranium"
    correct: true
  - text: Half the uranium is lost in mining
  - text: Uranium is heavier than coal
  - text: Enrichment wastes energy
  explanation: "**p. 161:** “(This 2 g of uranium is not as small as one millionth of 16 kg per day, by the way, because today’s reactors burn up less than 1% of the uranium.)”"
- id: q7
  prompt: How does MacKay describe the nuclear waste problem?
  options:
  - text: "A \"beautifully small\" problem — small doesn't mean no problem"
    correct: true
  - text: Unsolvable
  - text: No problem at all
  - text: Bigger than the CO2 problem
  explanation: "**p. 161:** “the fact that the nuclear waste stream is small doesn’t mean that it’s not a problem; it’s just a ‘beautifully small’ problem.”"
---

- Distinguish nuclear fission from fusion
- Compare the mass flows of fossil fuels and nuclear fuel per person

    correct: true

    <MarkdigVersion>1.6.0</MarkdigVersion>
    <YamlDotNetVersion>18.1.0</YamlDotNetVersion>
    <BunitVersion>2.14.0</BunitVersion>
  </PropertyGroup>

    <!-- Web -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly" Version="$(MicrosoftAspNetCoreVersion)" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Configuration" Version="$(MicrosoftExtensionsVersion)" />
    <PackageVersion Include="Microsoft.Extensions.Http" Version="$(MicrosoftExtensionsVersion)" />

    <!-- Content Processing -->
    <PackageVersion Include="Markdig" Version="$(MarkdigVersion)" />
    <PackageVersion Include="YamlDotNet" Version="$(YamlDotNetVersion)" />

    <!--
      Testing — Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP) only.

      xunit.v3 4.0 ships MTP v2 in the box and has dropped MTP v1. MTP v2 removed the
      VSTest bridge on the .NET 10 SDK, so the two VSTest-only packages that used to
      live here (xunit.runner.visualstudio, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk) are gone:

        - xunit.runner.visualstudio -> VSTest adapter. Only needed by VSTest-era
          runners; xunit.v3 carries its own MTP runner natively.
        - Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk    -> VSTest host. MTP test projects are plain
          executables and do not need it.

      `dotnet test` is switched into MTP mode by the "test" section in global.json.
      Fewer packages also means a faster restore, which matters because these tests
      are meant to run after every change.
    -->
    <PackageVersion Include="xunit.v3" Version="$(XunitVersion)" />
    <PackageVersion Include="bunit" Version="$(BunitVersion)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

FILE: export.sh
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ===========================================================================
# export.sh — Export git-tracked project files to docs/llm/dump.txt
#
# Blog posts (content/blog/*.md): only front matter is included; the
# markdown body is omitted to save context space. Every other git-tracked
# file is exported in full.
#
# Excluded from export:
#   - The docs/ directory itself (to avoid recursion / stale LLM context)
#   - Binary files (images, fonts, etc.)
#
# Usage:
#   bash export.sh            # writes docs/llm/dump.txt
#   bash export.sh -o out.txt # writes to a custom path
# ===========================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# ── Configuration ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

OUTPUT_FILE="docs/llm/dump.txt"
BLOG_DIR="content/blog"
SEPARATOR="-------------------------------------------------------------------------------"
WIDE_SEP="==============================================================================="

# Binary file extensions to skip (lowercase comparison)
BINARY_EXTENSIONS="png jpg jpeg gif ico bmp svg webp woff woff2 ttf eot otf mp3 mp4 wav ogg pdf zip tar gz"

# ── Parse arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        -o|--output)
            OUTPUT_FILE="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -h|--help)
            echo "Usage: bash export.sh [-o OUTPUT_FILE]"
            echo "  Exports git-tracked project files to docs/llm/dump.txt"
            echo "  Blog posts include front matter only (body omitted)."
            exit 0
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown argument: $1" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done

# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

is_binary_extension() {
    local file="$1"
    local ext="${file##*.}"
    ext="${ext,,}" # lowercase
    for bin_ext in $BINARY_EXTENSIONS; do
        if [[ "$ext" == "$bin_ext" ]]; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

is_blog_post() {
    local file="$1"
    [[ "$file" == ${BLOG_DIR}/*.md ]]
}

is_excluded_dir() {
    local file="$1"
    [[ "$file" == docs/* ]]
}

# Extract only the YAML front matter (between first --- and second ---).
# Prints the front matter block including delimiters.
extract_front_matter() {
    local file="$1"
    local in_front_matter=0
    local found_start=0

    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ "$found_start" -eq 0 && "$line" == "---" ]]; then
            found_start=1
            in_front_matter=1
            echo "$line"
            continue
        fi
        if [[ "$in_front_matter" -eq 1 && "$line" == "---" ]]; then
            echo "$line"
            return
        fi
        if [[ "$in_front_matter" -eq 1 ]]; then
            echo "$line"
        fi
    done < "$file"
}

# ── Collect git-tracked files ────────────────────────────────────────────────

mapfile -t ALL_FILES < <(git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard | sort)

# ── Counters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

total_files=0
blog_front_matter_only=0
full_content_files=0
binary_skipped=0

# ── Ensure output directory exists ───────────────────────────────────────────

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUTPUT_FILE")"

# ── Write output ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

{
    # Header
    echo "$WIDE_SEP"
    echo "PROJECT EXPORT: terlingua.github.io"
    echo "DATE: $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC')"
    echo "$WIDE_SEP"
    echo ""

    # Directory tree
    echo "$WIDE_SEP"
    echo "DIRECTORY TREE (all git-tracked files)"
    echo "$WIDE_SEP"
    echo ""

    # Use tree if available, otherwise fall back to a simple listing
    if command -v tree &>/dev/null; then
        # Build a temp file list for tree --fromfile
        printf '%s\n' "${ALL_FILES[@]}" | tree --fromfile --charset utf-8 -a 2>/dev/null || {
            # Fallback: just print the sorted file list as an indented tree
            echo "."
            printf '%s\n' "${ALL_FILES[@]}" | sed 's|^|├── |'
        }
    else
        echo "."
        printf '%s\n' "${ALL_FILES[@]}" | sed 's|^|├── |'
    fi

    echo ""

    # File contents
    for file in "${ALL_FILES[@]}"; do
        # Skip files in docs/ directory
        if is_excluded_dir "$file"; then
            continue
        fi

        # Skip binary files
        if is_binary_extension "$file"; then
            binary_skipped=$((binary_skipped + 1))
            total_files=$((total_files + 1))
            continue
        fi

        # Skip the export script itself
        if [[ "$file" == "export.sh" ]]; then
            # Still include it — it's useful context for the LLM
            :
        fi

        echo ""
        echo "$SEPARATOR"

        if is_blog_post "$file"; then
            # Blog post: front matter only
            echo "FILE: ${file}  [FRONT MATTER ONLY — body omitted to save context space]"
            echo "$SEPARATOR"
            extract_front_matter "$file"
            echo ""
            blog_front_matter_only=$((blog_front_matter_only + 1))
        else
            # All other files: full content
            echo "FILE: ${file}"
            echo "$SEPARATOR"
            cat "$file"
            echo ""
            full_content_files=$((full_content_files + 1))
        fi

        total_files=$((total_files + 1))
    done

    # Footer
    echo ""
    echo "$WIDE_SEP"
    echo "EXPORT COMPLETED"
    echo "Total Files Exported: ${total_files}"
    echo "  Blog posts (front matter only): ${blog_front_matter_only}"
    echo "  Full content files: ${full_content_files}"
    echo "  Binary files skipped: ${binary_skipped}"
    echo "Output File: ${OUTPUT_FILE}"
    echo "$WIDE_SEP"

} > "$OUTPUT_FILE"

echo "Export complete: ${OUTPUT_FILE}"
echo "  Total files: ${total_files}"
echo "  Blog posts (front matter only): ${blog_front_matter_only}"
echo "  Full content files: ${full_content_files}"
echo "  Binary files skipped: ${binary_skipped}"

FILE: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    # Rebuild daily at 6 AM UTC to publish scheduled posts
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: "pages"
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true
  # xunit.v3 pulls in Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.Telemetry. Opt out in CI.
  TESTINGPLATFORM_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: 1

jobs:
  build-and-deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: '10.0.x'

      - name: Restore .NET dependencies
        run: dotnet restore

      - name: Run content processor (markdown → JSON + HTML)
        run: dotnet run --project tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor -- --content-dir content/blog --output-dir src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot --authors-dir content/authors --books-dir content/books

      # ── Audio generation with caching ──────────────────────────────
      # Cache key is based on the content of all blog markdown files.
      # Exact hit  → all MP3s restored, ALL Python steps skipped.
      # Partial hit → most MP3s restored, only changed posts regenerated.
      # Miss        → full regeneration (first run or cache eviction).

      - name: Restore audio cache
        id: audio-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: .audio-cache
          key: audio-v1-${{ hashFiles('content/blog/**/*.md') }}
          restore-keys: |
            audio-v1-

      - name: Copy cached audio to output
        run: |
          mkdir -p src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data
          if [ -d .audio-cache ] && [ "$(ls -A .audio-cache 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            cp .audio-cache/*.mp3 src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data/ 2>/dev/null || true
            cp .audio-cache/audio-manifest.json src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data/ 2>/dev/null || true
            echo "Restored $(ls .audio-cache/*.mp3 2>/dev/null | wc -l) cached MP3 file(s)"
          else
            echo "No audio cache to restore"
          fi

      # All Python/audio steps are skipped on exact cache hit
      - name: Setup Python 3.12 (for TTS audio generation)
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Install system dependencies (espeak-ng + ffmpeg)
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y espeak-ng ffmpeg

      - name: Cache HuggingFace model
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/huggingface
          key: hf-kitten-tts-nano-0.8

      - name: Cache pip packages
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: pip-audio-${{ hashFiles('tools/requirements-audio.txt') }}
          restore-keys: |
            pip-audio-

      - name: Install Python audio dependencies
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          pip install onnxruntime
          pip install -r tools/requirements-audio.txt

      - name: Generate TTS audio (markdown → MP3)
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: python tools/generate_audio.py --content-dir content/blog --output-dir src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data --voice Bella --model KittenML/kitten-tts-nano-0.8

      - name: Update audio cache
        if: steps.audio-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p .audio-cache
          cp src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data/*.mp3 .audio-cache/ 2>/dev/null || true
          cp src/ObserverMagazine.Web/wwwroot/blog-data/audio-manifest.json .audio-cache/ 2>/dev/null || true
          echo "Cached $(ls .audio-cache/*.mp3 2>/dev/null | wc -l) MP3 file(s) for next build"

      # ── End audio generation ───────────────────────────────────────

      # Microsoft.Testing.Platform mode (opted in via global.json).
      # `dotnet test <path>` is no longer valid syntax; the target is named with
      # --solution / --project / --test-modules. MTP fails the run if zero tests
      # execute, so a silently empty run cannot pass CI.
      - name: Run tests
        run: dotnet test --solution ObserverMagazine.slnx --no-restore

      - name: Publish Blazor WASM
        run: dotnet publish src/ObserverMagazine.Web/ObserverMagazine.Web.csproj -c Release -o publish

      - name: Strip source map references from framework JS
        run: |
          find publish/wwwroot/_framework -name "*.js" -exec sed -i '/^\/\/# sourceMappingURL=/d' {} + 2>/dev/null || true
          find publish/wwwroot/_framework -name "*.js" -exec sed -i '/^\/\/@ sourceMappingURL=/d' {} + 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Prepare GitHub Pages artifacts
        run: |
          cp publish/wwwroot/.nojekyll publish/wwwroot/.nojekyll 2>/dev/null || touch publish/wwwroot/.nojekyll
          cp publish/wwwroot/index.html publish/wwwroot/404.html

      - name: Setup Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v6

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5
        with:
          path: publish/wwwroot

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5

FILE: README.md
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Terlingua Magazine

A free, open-source Blazor WebAssembly application deployed to GitHub Pages.

Built with **.NET 10** (LTS) and **C# 14**.

## Features

- **Blog** — Write posts in Markdown with YAML front matter; compiled to static JSON at build time
- **RSS Feed** — Auto-generated `feed.xml`
- **Books & Quizzes** — Multi-chapter books with single- and multiple-answer quizzes; reading progress stored in the browser (IndexedDB)
- **Responsive Tables** — Sortable, filterable data tables that work on mobile
- **Master-Detail Flow** — Click a list item to view full details
- **OpenTelemetry-ready Logging** — Structured logging via `ILogger`
- **Full Test Suite** — bUnit component tests + xUnit.net v3 integration tests, running on Microsoft.Testing.Platform

## Quick Start
```bash
# Restore & process blog posts and books
dotnet run --project tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor

# Run the app locally
dotnet run --project src/ObserverMagazine.Web

# Run all tests
dotnet test
```

## Books

Books live under `content/books/` and are compiled by the content processor into
`wwwroot/book-data/` (git-ignored) at build time.

```
content/books/
  blazor-basics/                  # book slug (lowercase, digits, hyphens)
    book.yml                      # title, author, summary, date, tags, image, draft
    01-getting-started/           # NN-chapter-slug; the number sets the order
      chapter.yml                 # title, summary, draft
      01-what-is-blazor.md        # NN-subchapter-slug.md
      02-project-structure.md
    02-components/
      ...
```

Chapters and subchapters are numbered 1, 2, 3… in the order of their prefixes, so gaps
(`01`, `05`, `10`) are fine. Drafts and future-dated books are skipped.

### Subchapter format

```markdown
---
title: What is Blazor WebAssembly?
questions:
  - id: runtime                   # optional, defaults to q1, q2…; keep stable once published
    prompt: Where does the C# code run?
    explanation: Shown after a correct answer.   # optional
    options:
      - text: On the server
      - text: In the browser
        correct: true
  - id: hosting
    prompt: Which statements are true?
    type: multiple                # optional: single | multiple
    options:
      - id: static                # optional, defaults to a, b, c…
        text: It can be served from GitHub Pages
        correct: true
      - text: It needs ASP.NET Core on the server
---
Markdown body…
```

- `type` is inferred when omitted: more than one correct option means `multiple`.
  Set `type: multiple` explicitly to use checkboxes even when only one option is correct.
- Prompts, options and explanations support Markdown (inline code, emphasis, links).
- Question and option ids are what reader progress is keyed on. Changing them resets
  progress for that question.
- Invalid content (no correct option, fewer than two options, unnumbered files, missing
  `chapter.yml`, bad YAML, duplicate ids) fails the build with a list of errors.

### Library

| Book | Slug | Focus |
|------|------|-------|
| Sustainable Energy — Without the Hot Air: A Quiz Companion | `sustainable-energy-without-the-hot-air` | Self-test companion to David MacKay's free book: 43 chapters mirroring its chapters and sections, page pointers, errata, quotes in every explanation |
| Nutrition Science: What We Know and What We Don't | `nutrition-science` | Evidence-graded diet and nutrition: energy, macro- and micronutrients, patterns, disease, life stages, food safety, myths |
| .NET 10 and Modern C# | `modern-dotnet` | SDK, C# 14, async, hosting, minimal APIs, EF Core 10, architecture, testing, AOT |
| Modern Web Development with Blazor | `modern-blazor` | Render modes, component reuse, forms, routing, state, interop, security, Hybrid |
| SOLID Principles in C# | `solid-principles` | The five principles, refactorings and trade-offs |
| Clean Code in C# | `clean-code` | Naming, functions, errors, classes, tests, smells, refactoring |
| Dapper: Fast, Honest Data Access | `dapper` | Queries, parameters, mapping, transactions, architecture, testing |
| The Databricks Data Intelligence Platform | `databricks-platform` | Spark, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, pipelines, jobs, SQL, MLflow, GenAI |
| Microsoft Azure for .NET Developers | `microsoft-azure` | Identity, compute, data, messaging, networking, Bicep, governance |
| Amazon Web Services for Builders | `amazon-web-services` | IAM, compute, storage, databases, integration, VPC, IaC, cost |
| Blazor WebAssembly Basics | `blazor-basics` | A short introduction |

Content guidelines for new sections:

- Open with a "Learning objectives" list and keep each section focused on one concept
- Prefer small, compilable code snippets with a language on every code fence
- Write three or more questions per section, mixing single- and multiple-answer questions,
  with an `explanation` on every question
- Vary the position of the correct option; the UI does not shuffle options
- Non-software books may grade claims by certainty; `nutrition-science` uses Established, Strong, Uncertain and Not supported, and cites sources at the end of each section
- Companion books to an existing work (such as `sustainable-energy-without-the-hot-air`) do not reproduce the source text: each section points to the source's pages, lists learning objectives and any errata, and every explanation quotes a short fragment of the source or its errata with a page reference
- Quote option text that YAML would read as a boolean, number or null (`"Yes"`, `"50"`), and avoid `yes`, `no`, `null`, `true` and `false` as ids
- Quote YAML values that contain `: `, ` #` or start with a backtick or `@`

### Progress and analytics

- A section is complete when every question has been answered correctly, or, if it has
  no questions, once it has been opened.
- Progress is saved per book in IndexedDB (`terlingua-books` database). If IndexedDB is
  unavailable (private browsing, blocked storage) the app falls back to in-memory
  storage and tells the reader that progress will not persist.
- When the analytics backend is reachable, the reader count of a book and of each
  section is shown. A reader is counted once per book and once per section, using the
  local progress record to avoid counting repeat visits. Quiz answers are sent as
  interaction events. Nothing is shown and nothing breaks when the backend is down.

## Testing

Tests run on **Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP)**, not VSTest. The opt-in lives in
`global.json`:

```json
{ "test": { "runner": "Microsoft.Testing.Platform" } }
```

Test projects are ordinary executables, so each one can also be run on its own:

```bash
# Whole solution
dotnet test --solution ObserverMagazine.slnx

# One project
dotnet test --project tests/ObserverMagazine.Web.Tests

# Filter by class, or by trait
dotnet test --filter-class ObserverMagazine.Web.Tests.Services.BlogServiceTests
dotnet test --filter-trait Category=Integration

# Run a test project directly, no dotnet test involved
dotnet run --project tests/ObserverMagazine.Integration.Tests
```

Run `dotnet test -?` from the repo root for the full option list, which is built
from whichever MTP extensions the test projects reference.

xUnit configuration for MTP lives in `testconfig.json` next to a test project
(not `xunit.runner.json`, which is the VSTest-era file).

@implements IDisposable
@inject IAnalyticsService Analytics
@inject ILogger<BlogTtsPlayer> Logger
@inject IJSRuntime Js

@if (!_hidden)
{
    <div class="tts-player">
        <span class="tts-icon" aria-hidden="true">🔊</span>
        <span class="tts-label">Listen to this post</span>

        @if (_useFallbackControls)
        {
            @* Fallback: custom play/pause + seek when native controls don't render *@
            <audio id="tts-audio-@Slug"
                   preload="metadata"
                   playsinline
                   src="blog-data/@(Slug).mp3"
                   style="display:none;">
                Your browser does not support audio playback.
            </audio>
            <div class="tts-fallback">
                <button class="tts-fallback-btn" @onclick="ToggleFallbackPlay">
                    @(_fallbackPlaying ? "⏸ Pause" : "▶ Play")
                </button>
                <input type="range" class="tts-fallback-seek"
                       min="0" max="@_fallbackDuration" step="1"
                       value="@_fallbackCurrentTime"
                       @oninput="OnSeek" />
                <span class="tts-fallback-time">@FormatTime(_fallbackCurrentTime)</span>
            </div>
        }
        else
        {
            @* Default: native browser audio controls *@
            <audio id="tts-audio-@Slug"
                   controls
                   preload="metadata"
                   playsinline
                   src="blog-data/@(Slug).mp3"
                   @onplay="OnPlay"
                   @onpause="OnPause"
                   @onended="OnEnded">
                Your browser does not support audio playback.
            </audio>
        }

        @* Playback speed selector — shared across both native and fallback modes *@
        <div class="tts-speed">
            <label class="tts-speed-label" for="tts-speed-@Slug">Speed</label>
            <select id="tts-speed-@Slug"
                    class="tts-speed-select"
                    value="@_currentRate.ToString("0.##")"
                    @onchange="OnSpeedChange">
                @foreach (var rate in PlaybackRates)
                {
                    <option value="@rate.ToString("0.##")"
                            selected="@(Math.Abs(rate - _currentRate) < 0.01)">
                        @(rate.ToString("0.##"))x
                    </option>
                }
            </select>
        </div>

        <a class="tts-direct-link" href="blog-data/@(Slug).mp3" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"
           title="Open audio file directly in a new tab">
            Open audio ↗
        </a>
    </div>
}

@code {
    /// <summary>Blog post slug — matches the MP3 filename in blog-data/</summary>
    [Parameter, EditorRequired]
    public string Slug { get; set; } = string.Empty;

    private bool _hidden;
    private bool _useFallbackControls;
    private bool _fallbackPlaying;
    private int _fallbackCurrentTime;
    private int _fallbackDuration = 1; // avoid div-by-zero on range
    private double _currentRate = 1.0;

    private Timer? _pollTimer;

    /// <summary>Available playback speed options.</summary>
    private static readonly double[] PlaybackRates = [0.75, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0];

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender)
        {
            try
            {
                // Check if the audio source is available at all
                var canPlay = await Js.InvokeAsync<bool>("observerAudio.checkAvailability",
                    $"tts-audio-{Slug}");
                if (!canPlay)
                {
                    _hidden = true;
                    StateHasChanged();
                    return;
                }

                // Restore saved playback rate from localStorage
                var savedRate = await Js.InvokeAsync<double>("observerAudio.getSavedPlaybackRate");
                if (savedRate > 0)
                {
                    _currentRate = savedRate;
                    await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerAudio.setPlaybackRate",
                        $"tts-audio-{Slug}", _currentRate);
                }

                // Check if native controls rendered properly (height > 0).
                // Chrome Android clips the controls to 0px height in some CSS scenarios.
                var controlsRendered = await Js.InvokeAsync<bool>("observerAudio.checkControlsRendered",
                    $"tts-audio-{Slug}");
                if (!controlsRendered)
                {
                    Logger.LogInformation("Native audio controls not rendered for {Slug}, using fallback", Slug);
                    _useFallbackControls = true;
                    StateHasChanged();

                    // After switching to fallback, get duration
                    await Task.Delay(100); // let DOM update
                    var dur = await Js.InvokeAsync<double>("observerAudio.getDuration", $"tts-audio-{Slug}");
                    if (dur > 0)
                        _fallbackDuration = (int)Math.Ceiling(dur);

                    // Re-apply playback rate after fallback switch (new audio element may have reset)
                    await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerAudio.setPlaybackRate",
                        $"tts-audio-{Slug}", _currentRate);

                    StateHasChanged();
                }
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                Logger.LogDebug(ex, "Audio availability check failed for {Slug}", Slug);
            }
        }
    }

    protected override void OnParametersSet()
    {
        _hidden = false;
        _useFallbackControls = false;
        _fallbackPlaying = false;
        _fallbackCurrentTime = 0;
    }

    // --- Speed control ---

    private async Task OnSpeedChange(ChangeEventArgs e)
    {
        if (double.TryParse(e.Value?.ToString(),
            System.Globalization.NumberStyles.Float,
            System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var rate) && rate >= 0.5 && rate <= 3.0)
        {
            _currentRate = rate;
            try
            {
                await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerAudio.setPlaybackRate", $"tts-audio-{Slug}", rate);
                await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerAudio.savePlaybackRate", rate);
                Logger.LogInformation("TTS speed changed to {Rate}x for {Slug}", rate, Slug);
                await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("TTS.SpeedChange", $"{Slug}:{rate}x");
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                Logger.LogDebug(ex, "Failed to set playback rate for {Slug}", Slug);
            }
        }
    }

    // --- Fallback controls ---

    private async Task ToggleFallbackPlay()
    {
        try
        {
            if (_fallbackPlaying)
            {
                await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerAudio.pause", $"tts-audio-{Slug}");
                _fallbackPlaying = false;
                StopPolling();
                await OnPause();
            }
            else
            {
                await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerAudio.play", $"tts-audio-{Slug}");
                _fallbackPlaying = true;
                StartPolling();
                await OnPlay();
            }
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            Logger.LogWarning(ex, "Fallback play/pause failed for {Slug}", Slug);
        }
    }

    private async Task OnSeek(ChangeEventArgs e)
    {
        if (double.TryParse(e.Value?.ToString(), out var time))
        {
            _fallbackCurrentTime = (int)time;
            try
            {
                await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerAudio.setCurrentTime", $"tts-audio-{Slug}", time);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                Logger.LogDebug(ex, "Seek failed for {Slug}", Slug);
            }
        }
    }

    private void StartPolling()
    {
        StopPolling();
        _pollTimer = new Timer(PollTimerCallback, null, TimeSpan.Zero, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(500));
    }

    /// <summary>
    /// Timer callback — uses async void because TimerCallback returns void.
    /// All async work is wrapped in try-catch to prevent unobserved exceptions.
    /// </summary>
    private async void PollTimerCallback(object? state)
    {
        try
        {
            var time = await Js.InvokeAsync<double>("observerAudio.getCurrentTime", $"tts-audio-{Slug}");
            var ended = await Js.InvokeAsync<bool>("observerAudio.hasEnded", $"tts-audio-{Slug}");
            await InvokeAsync(() =>
            {
                _fallbackCurrentTime = (int)time;
                if (ended)
                {
                    _fallbackPlaying = false;
                    StopPolling();
                    _ = OnEnded();
                }
                StateHasChanged();
            });
        }
        catch
        {
            // Component may have been disposed — ignore
        }
    }

    private void StopPolling()
    {
        _pollTimer?.Dispose();
        _pollTimer = null;
    }

    private static string FormatTime(int seconds)
    {
        var m = seconds / 60;
        var s = seconds % 60;
        return $"{m}:{s:D2}";
    }

    // --- Analytics events ---

    private async Task OnPlay()
    {
        Logger.LogInformation("TTS play: {Slug}", Slug);
        await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("TTS.Play", Slug);
    }

    private async Task OnPause()
    {
        Logger.LogInformation("TTS pause: {Slug}", Slug);
        await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("TTS.Pause", Slug);
    }

    private async Task OnEnded()
    {
        Logger.LogInformation("TTS finished: {Slug}", Slug);
        await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("TTS.Finished", Slug);
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        StopPolling();
    }
}

@inject HttpClient Http
@inject ILogger<MasterDetail> Logger
@inject IAnalyticsService Analytics
@inject IJSRuntime Js

@* ---- Confirmation dialog ---- *@
@if (_confirmAction is not null)
{
    <div class="confirm-overlay" @onclick="CancelConfirm">
        <div class="confirm-dialog" @onclick:stopPropagation="true">
            <h4>@_confirmTitle</h4>
            <p>@_confirmMessage</p>
            <div class="form-actions">
                <button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm" @onclick="CancelConfirm">Cancel</button>
                <button class="btn btn-danger btn-sm" @onclick="ExecuteConfirm">@_confirmButton</button>
            </div>

}

<div class="md-container">

                    {
                        <div class="form-validation">Name is required.</div>
                    }
                </div>

                              placeholder="Describe the product"></textarea>

                    <button class="btn btn-primary btn-sm" @onclick="SaveEdit">Save</button>
                    <button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm" @onclick="CancelEdit">Cancel</button>
                </div>

@code {
    private const string StorageKey = "observer-products-v1";

    private enum ViewMode { Idle, Viewing, Editing, Adding }

    private List<Product>? _products;
    private Product? _selected;
    private ViewMode _viewMode = ViewMode.Idle;

    // Edit form fields
    private string _editName = "";
    private string _editCategory = "";
    private decimal _editPrice;
    private int _editStock;
    private double _editRating;
    private string _editDescription = "";
    private bool _showValidation;

    // Confirmation dialog
    private string _confirmTitle = "";
    private string _confirmMessage = "";
    private string _confirmButton = "";
    private Func<Task>? _confirmAction;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        Logger.LogInformation("Loading product data for master-detail");
        await LoadProducts();
    }

    private async Task LoadProducts()
    {
        try
        {
            // Try localStorage first
            var saved = await Js.InvokeAsync<string?>("localStorage.getItem", StorageKey);
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(saved))
            {
                _products = System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Deserialize<List<Product>>(saved,
                    new System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true });
                Logger.LogInformation("Loaded {Count} products from local storage", _products?.Count ?? 0);
            }
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            Logger.LogDebug(ex, "Could not read from local storage");
        }

        if (_products is null || _products.Count == 0)
        {
            try
            {
                var loaded = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<Product[]>("sample-data/products.json");
                _products = loaded?.ToList() ?? [];
                Logger.LogInformation("Loaded {Count} products from JSON", _products.Count);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                Logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to load products");
                _products = [];
            }
        }
    }

    private async Task SaveProducts()
    {
        if (_products is null) return;
        try
        {
            var json = System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(_products,
                new System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNamingPolicy = System.Text.Json.JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase });
            await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("localStorage.setItem", StorageKey, json);
            Logger.LogInformation("Saved {Count} products to local storage", _products.Count);
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            Logger.LogWarning(ex, "Could not save to local storage");
        }
    }

    private async Task SelectProduct(Product product)
    {
        if (_viewMode is ViewMode.Editing or ViewMode.Adding) return;
        _selected = product;
        _viewMode = ViewMode.Viewing;
        Logger.LogInformation("Selected product: {Name}", product.Name);
        await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("ProductSelect", product.Name);
    }

    // ---- CRUD operations ----

    private void StartAdd()
    {
        _selected = null;
        _editName = "";
        _editCategory = "";
        _editPrice = 0;
        _editStock = 0;
        _editRating = 0;
        _editDescription = "";
        _showValidation = false;
        _viewMode = ViewMode.Adding;
    }

    private void StartEdit()
    {
        if (_selected is null) return;
        _editName = _selected.Name;
        _editCategory = _selected.Category;
        _editPrice = _selected.Price;
        _editStock = _selected.Stock;
        _editRating = _selected.Rating;
        _editDescription = _selected.Description;
        _showValidation = false;
        _viewMode = ViewMode.Editing;
    }

    private async Task SaveEdit()
    {
        _showValidation = true;
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_editName)) return;

        if (_viewMode == ViewMode.Adding)
        {
            var newProduct = new Product
            {
                Id = Guid.NewGuid(),
                Name = _editName.Trim(),
                Category = _editCategory.Trim(),
                Price = _editPrice,
                Stock = _editStock,
                Rating = Math.Clamp(_editRating, 0, 5),
                Description = _editDescription.Trim()
            };
            _products!.Add(newProduct);
            _selected = newProduct;
            Logger.LogInformation("Added product: {Name}", newProduct.Name);
            await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("ProductAdd", newProduct.Name);
        }
        else if (_viewMode == ViewMode.Editing && _selected is not null)
        {
            var idx = _products!.FindIndex(p => p.Id == _selected.Id);
            if (idx >= 0)
            {
                var updated = _selected with
                {
                    Name = _editName.Trim(),
                    Category = _editCategory.Trim(),
                    Price = _editPrice,
                    Stock = _editStock,
                    Rating = Math.Clamp(_editRating, 0, 5),
                    Description = _editDescription.Trim()
                };
                _products[idx] = updated;
                _selected = updated;
                Logger.LogInformation("Updated product: {Name}", updated.Name);
                await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("ProductUpdate", updated.Name);
            }
        }

        await SaveProducts();
        _viewMode = ViewMode.Viewing;
        _showValidation = false;
    }

    private void CancelEdit()
    {
        _viewMode = _selected is not null ? ViewMode.Viewing : ViewMode.Idle;
        _showValidation = false;
    }

    private void ConfirmDelete()
    {
        if (_selected is null) return;
        _confirmTitle = "Delete Product";
        _confirmMessage = $"Are you sure you want to delete \"{_selected.Name}\"? This cannot be undone.";
        _confirmButton = "Delete";
        _confirmAction = ExecuteDelete;
    }

    private async Task ExecuteDelete()
    {
        if (_selected is not null && _products is not null)
        {
            var name = _selected.Name;
            _products.RemoveAll(p => p.Id == _selected.Id);
            _selected = null;
            _viewMode = ViewMode.Idle;
            await SaveProducts();
            Logger.LogInformation("Deleted product: {Name}", name);
            await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("ProductDelete", name);
        }
        _confirmAction = null;
    }

    private void ConfirmReset()
    {
        _confirmTitle = "Reset to Defaults";
        _confirmMessage = "This will discard all your changes and restore the original product data. Continue?";
        _confirmButton = "Reset";
        _confirmAction = ExecuteReset;
    }

    private async Task ExecuteReset()
    {
        try
        {
            await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("localStorage.removeItem", StorageKey);
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            Logger.LogDebug(ex, "Could not clear local storage");
        }

        _products = null;
        _selected = null;
        _viewMode = ViewMode.Idle;
        await LoadProducts();
        Logger.LogInformation("Reset products to defaults");
        await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("ProductReset", "");
        _confirmAction = null;
    }

    private void CancelConfirm()
    {
        _confirmAction = null;
    }

    private async Task ExecuteConfirm()
    {
        if (_confirmAction is not null)
        {
            await _confirmAction();
        }
    }
}

    <ul class="quiz-options">

    <div class="quiz-actions">
        @if (_result is null)
        {
            <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary btn-sm quiz-submit" disabled="@(_selected.Count == 0)" @onclick="SubmitAsync">
                Check answer
            </button>
        }
        else if (!_result.IsCorrect)
        {
            <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline btn-sm quiz-retry" @onclick="Retry">Try again</button>
            if (!_revealed)
            {
                <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline btn-sm quiz-reveal" @onclick="Reveal">Show answer</button>
            }
        }
        @if (_attempts > 0)
        {
            <span class="quiz-attempts">@_attempts @(_attempts == 1 ? "attempt" : "attempts")</span>
        }
    </div>

    @if (_result is not null)
    {
        <div class="quiz-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite">
            @if (_result.IsCorrect)
            {
                <strong class="quiz-verdict">Correct!</strong>
            }
            else
            {
                <strong class="quiz-verdict">Not quite.</strong>
                if (Question.MultipleAnswers && !_revealed)
                {
                    <span> Select every correct answer and nothing else.</span>
                }
            }
            @if (ShowSolution && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(Question.ExplanationHtml))
            {
                <div class="quiz-explanation">@((MarkupString)Question.ExplanationHtml)</div>
            }
        </div>
    }
</fieldset>

@code {
    [Parameter, EditorRequired] public QuizQuestion Question { get; set; } = null!;
    [Parameter] public int Number { get; set; } = 1;
    [Parameter] public QuestionProgress? InitialProgress { get; set; }
    [Parameter] public EventCallback<QuizAnswer> OnAnswered { get; set; }

    private readonly HashSet<string> _selected = new(StringComparer.Ordinal);
    private QuizResult? _result;
    private bool _revealed;
    private int _attempts;

    private string ElementId => $"quiz-{Question.Id}";
    private bool IsLocked => _result is not null;
    private bool ShowSolution => _result is { IsCorrect: true } || _revealed;

    private string StateClass => _result switch
    {
        null => "",
        { IsCorrect: true } => "is-correct",
        _ => "is-incorrect"
    };

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        if (InitialProgress is null)
        {
            return;
        }

        _attempts = InitialProgress.Attempts;
        if (!InitialProgress.LastAttemptCorrect)
        {
            return;
        }

        var restored = QuizEvaluator.Evaluate(Question, InitialProgress.LastSelection);
        if (restored.IsCorrect)
        {
            _selected.UnionWith(restored.Selected);
            _result = restored;
        }
    }

    private string OptionClass(QuizOption option)
    {
        var classes = new List<string> { "quiz-option" };
        if (_selected.Contains(option.Id))
        {
            classes.Add("is-selected");
        }

        if (_result is not null)
        {
            if (ShowSolution && option.Correct)
            {
                classes.Add("is-answer");
            }
            if (_result.IsWronglySelected(option.Id))
            {
                classes.Add("is-wrong");
            }
        }

        return string.Join(' ', classes);
    }

    private void OnOptionChanged(string optionId, ChangeEventArgs e)
    {
        if (IsLocked)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (!Question.MultipleAnswers)
        {
            _selected.Clear();
            _selected.Add(optionId);
            return;
        }

        var isChecked = e.Value switch
        {
            bool b => b,
            string s => bool.TryParse(s, out var parsed) && parsed,
            _ => false
        };

        if (isChecked)
        {
            _selected.Add(optionId);
        }
        else
        {
            _selected.Remove(optionId);
        }
    }

    private async Task SubmitAsync()
    {
        if (_selected.Count == 0 || _result is not null)
        {
            return;
        }

        _result = QuizEvaluator.Evaluate(Question, _selected);
        _attempts++;
        await OnAnswered.InvokeAsync(new QuizAnswer(Question, _selected.ToArray(), _result));
    }

    private void Retry()
    {
        _result = null;
        _revealed = false;
        _selected.Clear();
    }

    private void Reveal() => _revealed = true;
}

@inject IAnalyticsService Analytics

@if (_reactions is not null)
{
    <div class="reactions-bar">
        @foreach (var (emoji, type) in ReactionTypes)
        {
            var count = _reactions.GetValueOrDefault(type, 0);
            <button class="reaction-btn @(_userReacted == type ? "reacted" : "")"
                    @onclick="() => React(type)"
                    title="@type">
                <span class="reaction-emoji">@emoji</span>
                @if (count > 0)
                {
                    <span class="reaction-count">@count</span>
                }
            </button>
        }
    </div>
}

@code {
    [Parameter] public string Slug { get; set; } = "";

    private static readonly (string Emoji, string Type)[] ReactionTypes =
    [
        ("👍", "like"),
        ("❤️", "love"),
        ("🎉", "celebrate"),
        ("🤔", "thinking")
    ];

    private Dictionary<string, int>? _reactions;
    private string? _userReacted;

    protected override async Task OnParametersSetAsync()
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(Slug)) return;

        _reactions = await Analytics.GetReactionsAsync(Slug);
        // If backend returned null, reactions stays null and the UI is hidden
    }

    private async Task React(string type)
    {
        if (_reactions is null || _userReacted == type) return;

        _userReacted = type;
        await Analytics.AddReactionAsync(Slug, type);

        // Optimistic update
        _reactions[type] = _reactions.GetValueOrDefault(type, 0) + 1;
        await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("Reaction", $"{Slug}: {type}");
    }
}

@inject HttpClient Http
@inject ILogger<ResponsiveTable> Logger
@inject IAnalyticsService Analytics

@if (_products is null)
{
    <p><em>Loading data...</em></p>
}
else
{
    <div class="rt-controls">
        <input type="text"
               placeholder="Filter by name..."
               @bind="_filterText"
               @bind:event="oninput"
               class="rt-filter-input" />
    </div>

    <div class="rt-table-responsive">
        <table class="rt-data-table">
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th class="rt-sortable" @onclick='() => Sort("Name")'>
                        Name @SortIndicator("Name")
                    </th>
                    <th class="rt-sortable" @onclick='() => Sort("Category")'>
                        Category @SortIndicator("Category")
                    </th>
                    <th class="rt-sortable rt-numeric" @onclick='() => Sort("Price")'>
                        Price @SortIndicator("Price")
                    </th>
                    <th class="rt-sortable rt-numeric" @onclick='() => Sort("Stock")'>
                        Stock @SortIndicator("Stock")
                    </th>
                    <th>Rating</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                @foreach (var p in FilteredAndSorted)
                {
                    <tr>
                        <td data-label="Name">@p.Name</td>
                        <td data-label="Category">@p.Category</td>
                        <td data-label="Price" class="rt-numeric">@p.Price.ToString("C")</td>
                        <td data-label="Stock" class="rt-numeric">@p.Stock</td>
                        <td data-label="Rating">
                            @for (int i = 0; i < (int)Math.Round(p.Rating); i++)
                            {
                                <span class="rt-star">★</span>
                            }
                        </td>
                    </tr>
                }
            </tbody>
        </table>
    </div>

    <p class="rt-info">
        Showing @FilteredAndSorted.Count() of @_products.Length items
    </p>
}

@code {
    private Product[]? _products;
    private string _filterText = "";
    private string _sortColumn = "Name";
    private bool _sortAscending = true;

    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        Logger.LogInformation("Loading product data for responsive table");
        try
        {
            _products = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<Product[]>("sample-data/products.json");
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            Logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to load products");
            _products = [];
        }
    }

    private IEnumerable<Product> FilteredAndSorted
    {
        get
        {
            if (_products is null) return [];

            var filtered = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_filterText)
                ? _products.AsEnumerable()
                : _products.Where(p =>
                    p.Name.Contains(_filterText, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

            return _sortColumn switch
            {
                "Name" => _sortAscending ? filtered.OrderBy(p => p.Name) : filtered.OrderByDescending(p => p.Name),
                "Category" => _sortAscending ? filtered.OrderBy(p => p.Category) : filtered.OrderByDescending(p => p.Category),
                "Price" => _sortAscending ? filtered.OrderBy(p => p.Price) : filtered.OrderByDescending(p => p.Price),
                "Stock" => _sortAscending ? filtered.OrderBy(p => p.Stock) : filtered.OrderByDescending(p => p.Stock),
                _ => filtered
            };
        }
    }

    private async Task Sort(string column)
    {
        if (_sortColumn == column)
        {
            _sortAscending = !_sortAscending;
        }
        else
        {
            _sortColumn = column;
            _sortAscending = true;
        }
        Logger.LogInformation("Sorted by {Column} {Direction}", column, _sortAscending ? "asc" : "desc");
        await Analytics.TrackInteractionAsync("TableSort", $"{column} {(_sortAscending ? "asc" : "desc")}");
    }

    private string SortIndicator(string column)
    {
        if (_sortColumn != column) return "";
        return _sortAscending ? "▲" : "▼";
    }
}

@inject IJSRuntime Js
@inject ILogger<RichContent> Logger

<div class="blog-content">
    @((MarkupString)_processedHtml)
</div>

@code {
    [Parameter, EditorRequired] public string Html { get; set; } = "";

    private string _processedHtml = "";
    private string? _sourceHtml;
    private bool _enhancementPending;

    protected override void OnParametersSet()
    {
        if (string.Equals(_sourceHtml, Html, StringComparison.Ordinal))
        {
            return;
        }

        _sourceHtml = Html;
        _processedHtml = HtmlPostProcessor.Process(Html);
        _enhancementPending = true;
    }

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (!_enhancementPending)
        {
            return;
        }

        _enhancementPending = false;
        try
        {
            await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerHighlight.highlightAll");
            await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerCodeScroll.init");
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            Logger.LogDebug(ex, "Post-render content enhancement failed");
        }
    }
}

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
@inject IReadingProgressService ProgressService
@inject IBookAnalytics BookAnalytics

@if (Content.Questions.Length > 0)
{
    <section class="subchapter-quiz" aria-labelledby="quiz-heading">
        <header class="quiz-header">
            <h2 id="quiz-heading">Check your understanding</h2>
            <span class="quiz-score">@CorrectCount of @Content.Questions.Length answered correctly</span>
        </header>

        @for (var i = 0; i < Content.Questions.Length; i++)
        {
            var question = Content.Questions[i];
            var number = i + 1;
            <QuizQuestionCard @key="question.Id"
                              Question="question"
                              Number="number"
                              InitialProgress="GetQuestionProgress(question.Id)"
                              OnAnswered="HandleAnsweredAsync" />
        }

        @if (CorrectCount == Content.Questions.Length)
        {
            <p class="quiz-complete" role="status">Nice work, you have completed this section.</p>
        }
    </section>
}

@code {
    [Parameter, EditorRequired] public string BookSlug { get; set; } = "";
    [Parameter, EditorRequired] public SubchapterContent Content { get; set; } = null!;
    [Parameter] public SubchapterProgress? Progress { get; set; }
    [Parameter] public EventCallback<BookProgress> OnProgressChanged { get; set; }

    private int CorrectCount => Progress is { } progress
        ? Content.Questions.Count(q => progress.Questions.TryGetValue(q.Id, out var p) && p.AnsweredCorrectly)
        : 0;

    private QuestionProgress? GetQuestionProgress(string questionId) =>
        Progress?.Questions.GetValueOrDefault(questionId);

    private async Task HandleAnsweredAsync(QuizAnswer answer)
    {
        var progress = await ProgressService.RecordAnswerAsync(
            BookSlug,
            Content.ChapterSlug,
            Content.Slug,
            answer.Question.Id,
            answer.SelectedOptionIds,
            answer.Result.IsCorrect);

        await OnProgressChanged.InvokeAsync(progress);
        await BookAnalytics.RecordQuizAnswerAsync(BookSlug, Content.ChapterSlug, Content.Slug, answer.Question.Id, answer.Result.IsCorrect);
    }
}

                </svg>
            </a>
        </li>

            <select class="theme-select"
                    value="@_currentTheme"
                    @onchange="OnThemeChanged"
                    aria-label="Choose theme">
                <option value="system">System</option>
                <option value="light">Light</option>
                <option value="dark">Dark</option>
                <option value="sepia">Sepia</option>
                <option value="solarized-light">Solarized Light</option>

@code {
    private bool _isOpen;
    private string _currentTheme = "system";

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        Nav.LocationChanged += OnLocationChanged;
    }

    private void ToggleMenu() => _isOpen = !_isOpen;

    private void CloseMenu() => _isOpen = false;

    private void OnLocationChanged(object? sender, LocationChangedEventArgs e)
    {
        if (_isOpen)
        {
            _isOpen = false;
            InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged);
        }
    }

    protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (firstRender)
        {
            _currentTheme = await Js.InvokeAsync<string>("observerTheme.get");
            StateHasChanged();
        }
    }

    private async Task OnThemeChanged(ChangeEventArgs e)
    {
        _currentTheme = e.Value?.ToString() ?? "system";
        await Js.InvokeVoidAsync("observerTheme.set", _currentTheme);
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        Nav.LocationChanged -= OnLocationChanged;
    }
}
